Random noise, structural shifts, or unforeseen developments could all contribute to outcomes deviating more widely from the central estimate.

There are specific risks or events that could push the actual outcomes outside the stated confidence intervals. Similarly, unforeseen technological or policy changes could rapidly alter the trajectory in unexpected ways, particularly at the 1-week or 1-month horizons where there's more time for external disruptions to have an effect. Such risks are difficult to quantify exactly within the model but are important to remain aware of when interpreting these probabilistic forecasts.
